name: Indianapolis International
subtitle: Stand assignment and push control for the FedEx hub ramp
source: Stand numbers, layout, headings and ramp spots from the user-supplied KIND FedEx ramp diagrams (two sheets). No coordinates were given, so each sheet's background map was fitted to OpenStreetMap taxiway lines (about 0.81 m per diagram pixel; the runway 23L and 32 thresholds land within about 10 m), then each sheet's drawn layout was moved as a whole (east sheet 33 m NE, west sheet 30 m W) to sit best on the real OSM lead-in lines of the same numbers. Spot 5, drawn on both sheets, then agrees to 13 m and sits at the midpoint. Stands sit a median of about 12 m from an OSM lead-in line. Each stand is 20 m back from the nose end of its drawn lead-in line; even-numbered rows nose southeast and odd-numbered rows northwest, as drawn. Taxiways, aprons and buildings are from OpenStreetMap (© OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL). The chart frame is generated: north up, 1.5 m per pixel, linear in lat/lon.

positions.name: FedEx Ramp
positions.note: The diagrams give no ramp frequency, so the stand telex has no CTC line.

airlinesSource: FedEx (FDX) and flights with FEDEX in remarks park on the hub ramp. Other operators are not given out automatically.
notes: Spots from the diagrams: 2, 4, 6 and 8 are in only; 3, 5 and 7 are out only; 1, 7E and 7W are in and out. Arrivals are told their in spot, departures their out spot.
No ramp frequency on the diagrams, so telexes carry no CTC line.
